proofs.full_local_argument: Fix x0 in X. Strong convexity gives g(x0,y)>=g(x0,0)+g_y(x0,0)^T y+(mu_g/2)||y||_2^2. Therefore g(x0,.) is coercive and continuous, so a minimizer exists on R^m; strict convexity makes it unique, denoted y0. Unconstrained optimality gives g_y(x0,y0)=0. Define F(x,y)=g_y(x,y). It is C^1 near (x0,y0), and D_yF=H(x0,y0) is invertible because H>=mu_g I. The implicit function theorem supplies a local C^1 map psi with F(x,psi(x))=0 and psi(x0)=y0. For nearby x in X, strong convexity makes every stationary point the unique global minimizer; hence psi(x)=y*(x). Differentiating F(x,psi(x))=0 yields A(x,psi(x))^T+H(x,psi(x))Dpsi(x)=0. Thus Dy*(x)=-H^-1 A^T=-M^T. This supplies the stated local extension at boundary points. The chain rule yields grad Phi=f_x+(Dy*)^T f_y=f_x-AH^-1 f_y, since H is symmetric. Since x0 was arbitrary, the identities hold for every x in X in this sense.
proofs.omitted_details: None beyond the standard implicit function theorem, chain rule and finite-dimensional compactness.

assumptions: n,m are positive finite integers. X is a nonempty closed convex subset of R^n. The lower minimization is unconstrained over R^m. f is C^1 and g is C^2 on an open neighborhood of X times R^m; this explicitly states the local smooth-extension interpretation used for differentiation at boundary points.
Assumption 1(a): uniformly for x in X, f_x(x,.) and f_y(x,.) are Lipschitz in y with finite positive L_fx,L_fy.
Assumption 1(b): ||f_y(x,y)||_2<=C_fy for all x in X,y in R^m, with finite C_fy>0.
Assumption 1(c): uniformly in y, f_y(.,y) is Lipschitz on X with finite positive barL_fy.
Assumption 2(a): g is continuously twice differentiable in (x,y).
Assumption 2(b): uniformly in x, g_y(x,.) is Lipschitz with finite positive L_g.
Assumption 2(c): g(x,.) is mu_g-strongly convex on R^m for every x in X, with common mu_g>0; H(x,y)>=mu_g I.
Assumption 2(d): uniformly in x, A(x,.) and H(x,.) are Lipschitz in y with finite positive L_gxy,L_gyy.

Assumption 2(f): uniformly in y, A(.,y) and H(.,y) are Lipschitz on X with finite positive barL_gxy,barL_gyy. Matrix bounds can be read in induced 2-norm; Frobenius bounds suffice as upper bounds. Full standing assumptions are retained, with no minimal-assumption claim.
statement.conclusion: y*(x) exists uniquely and is locally C^1 in the implicit-extension sense. Dy*(x)=-H(x,y*(x))^-1 A(x,y*(x))^T=-M(x,y*(x))^T. grad Phi(x)=f_x(x,y*(x))-A(x,y*(x))H(x,y*(x))^-1 f_y(x,y*(x)).
statement.objects_and_definitions: Phi(x)=f(x,y*(x)); y*(x)=argmin_{y in R^m}g(x,y). Column gradients: A=g_xy in R^{n x m}, H=g_yy in R^{m x m}, M=AH^-1, and Dy* in R^{m x n}. At boundary points of X, derivatives mean the local implicit-function extension described in the argument.
statement.parameter_domains: n,m positive finite integers; mu_g>0; every named regularity constant finite and positive.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every x in X, deterministically. Boundary derivatives refer to a local implicit extension.
